Buyer's agents are typically paid out of the total commission dollars available, which the seller pays. In other words, they split the fee paid with the listing agent. The buyer's agent (if you've found your house) assists you in making your deal, helps you with things like escrow, contracts, home warranties and title insurance, and "runs" the whole transaction for you. As real estate and the contracts that go with it have become more and more complex, it's a needed part of the transaction. In addition, the buyer's agent is ON YOUR SIDE, and has a much stronger connection with you. He's required by law to look out for your best interests, while if you buy a home without the aid of a buyer's agent, you are risking having no representation at all. Some states now require both seller's and buyer's agents, because of the potential conflict of interest when both sides are represented. I am retired now but I was a real estate agent for many years. Ask away.

The buyer's agent splits the commission with the seller's agent. The agent handles the complex homebuying process, helps locate houses for you, pesters sellers and their agents, makes sure all of the necessary paperwork is submitted and signed, etc.

Unless someone is experienced at home-buying (it sounds like your mother is not), they should absolutely use an agent.
